body.content: Wait, check collinearity for 6+6+1. Points: (0.2, 0), (0.4, 0), (0.5, 0.5). These are not collinear. What about (0.2, 1), (0.2, 0), (0.5, 0.5)? Not collinear. What about (0,0), (0.2, 0), (0.4, 0)? These ARE collinear. But they are on the boundary. The checker looks at ALL triples. Three points on the same boundary line form a triangle of area 0. The claim-honest predicate requires `min(...) >= float(cl[-1])`. If the min area is 0, the claim is 0. The floor is 0.005. So this configuration FAILS the floor because of the boundary points! We cannot have 3 points on the same straight line.
body.possible_next_move: Perturb the boundary points to avoid collinearity. E.g., use a slight curve or alternate y-values (y=0, y=1e-6). But the checker might use exact float comparison. Better: use points strictly inside or distribute them to avoid 3 points on any line.
body.why_keep_this: CRITICAL FLAW: Boundary-heavy configurations with >2 points on a single edge will contain collinear triples, resulting in a minimum area of 0 and failing the 0.005 floor. Boundary points must be perturbed or limited to 2 per edge.
